sources.entry: Squid - Caching proxy for the Web supporting HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and more. It reduces bandwidth and improves response times by caching and reusing frequently-requested web pages. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.name: Squid
summary.one_liner: Squid is a caching proxy server for web clients that handles HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP traffic, and this Launchpad page is a git mirror of its source repository.
use_cases: Reduce bandwidth use by caching frequently requested web pages
Speed up web response times for a network
Proxy and log HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP traffic
Apply access controls to web traffic
Browse or build the Squid source code from a git mirror
summary.what_it_does: Squid is a proxy caching server for web clients that supports HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP data objects over IPv4 or IPv6. According to the listing, it handles all requests in a single non-blocking asynchronous process and keeps metadata and hot objects cached in RAM. It also caches DNS lookups, supports non-blocking DNS, and implements negative caching of failed requests. The page itself is a Launchpad git repository mirror showing branches (such as v7, master, v6, v5) and recent commits, imported from the GitHub squid-cache repository.
notable: Single non-blocking asynchronous process for all requests
Keeps hot objects and metadata cached in RAM and caches DNS lookups
Supports TLS, extensive access controls, and full request logging
Licensed GPL-2.0 and written in C
caveats: This page is a git mirror on Launchpad; the upstream project lives on GitHub
Platform list is partly inferred: Windows appears only through the mswin and mingw branch names, and Linux through the Debian (deb) listing
